text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO BREACH detected for /v1/generate in channel eng-runtime. p99 decode latency 2.6s (threshold 1.5s) over last 5m. Affected region: us-west-2. Affected model: redwood-34b-quant-v2-compile. Pager: @oncall-robert

oncall-robert: paging in, looking.

sara: seeing streaming stalls and long tail on decode step, p95 up to 800ms but p99 spikes well over 2s. logs show "decode_kernel: compile_path=trt_flashattn_v2 flag: -O3 -fast-math".

mike: correlated with last deploy at 2026-03-12 08:12 UTC — kernel rollout of trt_flashattn_v2. Rolling back is an option.

jin: attaching snip of error logs: ```ERROR decode failed: kernel_timeout 3000ms stack:... kernel=trt_flashattn_v2``` 

alice: customer-facing SLO dashboard shows spike for a handful of customers — 4 tenants > 5% error/slow. Opening incident channel? we're already here.

ryan: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pin requests to redwood-34b-quant-v1-legacy compile 2) disable continuous batching for affected pool 3) increase token timeout for streaming to 10s 4) start trace capture.

oncall-robert: executing step 1 now — switching routing policy to prefer legacy compile variant for us-west-2. Command: ```curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/routing -d '{"route":"redwood-34b-quant-v1-legacy","region":"us-west-2"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'``` 

ops-bot: ROUTE UPDATE succeeded. Active route now redwood-34b-quant-v1-legacy for 6 nodes in us-west-2.

sara: p99 dropped to 1.4s in the first 2 minutes after routing change. p95 stable at 420ms. Nice.

mike: we should still root cause. CI deployed a kernel build with new nvptx/flashattn kernels and changed compiler flag -ftree-vectorize and also bumped TRT minor. suspect vectorization or kernel codegen causing worst-case stall on specific token lengths.

jin: reproducer: running load test with sequence length distribution skewed to 1024 tokens triggers stall locally with trt_flashattn_v2. command: ```python perf_test.py --model redwood-34b --kernel trt_flashattn_v2 --seq-len 1024 --concurrency 8``` logs: ```stall at decode step 187 ms -> 2.3s```

alice: customer comms: flagged customers with support tags and sent note to CSMs. No escalations yet.

ryan: propose two-pronged fix: 1) rollback kernel rollout globally until we can validate microbenchmarks 2) add a compile-flag gate in CI that runs tail-latency tests for seq lengths 512/1024/2048.

oncall-robert: agreed. I'll open rollback PR. starting the rollback to previous kernel build across canaries.

ops-bot: ROLLBACK started for cluster us-west-2, target kernel redwood-kernel-v1. ETA ~ 7 minutes.

sara: monitoring: p99 trending down to 900ms now. streaming stalls dropped. Keep an eye on p95 too.

mike: capture and upload flamegraph/kv cache traces. Jin, can you capture kernel telemetry and kernel compile artifacts? We need the PTX and assembly diffs.

jin: on it. uploading to /mnt/artifacts/incident/1766504321. Noted a miscompiled matmul kernel when -ffast-math enabled; probably caused denorms to behave poorly.

alice: PM note: schedule a rollback postmortem and include customer impact list. Also block re-rollout until engineering triage and perf regression ticket done.

oncall-robert: handoff: I'm going to sleep, @mike you'll be primary for next 12h. Leaving runbook notes and commands in thread.

mike: taking handoff. I'll follow up with triage doc and open perf-regression ticket linking artifacts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated — SLO back within limits for us-west-2 after route rollback. Please update severity and notes.

alice: will schedule follow-up call with ML infra and compiler teams at 09:00 UTC to review kernel artifacts.

mike: adding final notes: root cause suspected: new trt_flashattn_v2 kernel + compiler flags (-O3 -ffast-math -ftree-vectorize) produced pathological kernel for certain seq lengths causing decode stalls. Action items: revert rollout, add tail-latency gate, add kernel canary with seq-length stress, update docs. Closing thread after postmortem.
